Explain how a siphon transfers water between two containers, why the outlet must be lower than the source surface, and how air entering the tube can interrupt flow. Use plain accurate prose. Aim for approximately 120–170 English tokens.

message.content: A siphon moves water through a tube that rises above the source surface, then bends down to an outlet. Gravity pulls water down the longer outlet leg. This creates lower pressure at the top of the tube, so atmospheric pressure pushes water up from the source. The water’s continuous cohesion and the pressure difference sustain flow. The outlet must be lower than the source surface so the downward leg has more gravitational potential to drive the process; if it is higher, gravity cannot pull water through, and flow stops or reverses. If air enters the tube, it breaks the continuous water column. Because air is compressible, the pressure difference cannot pull water past the bubble, so flow is interrupted.
